https://engineeringevil.com/2013/06/08/m.text: Home › Military Intelligence › ‘Missile defense killer’: Russia finalizes testing on prototype ICBM ‘Missile defense killer’: Russia finalizes testing on prototype ICBM By Ralph Turchiano on June 8, 2013 Published time: June 08, 2013 14:08 The high-speed lift of the Topol missile launching. (RIA Novosti / Vladimir Rodionov) Russia’s Strategic Missile Forces have reported a successful launch of a next-generation ICBM that can supposedly pierce any anti-ballistic missile (ABM) system. The test came after the US announced it would resume its ABM program in Europe. The test missile launched from a mobile pad at 9:45pm (17:45 GMT) on Thursday, the Defense Ministry said Friday. The test was carried out in the Astrakhan region, deep inside Russian territory, and the prototype’s payload successfully hit the Balkhash range in Kazakhstan. “The test launch was a success as the [simulated] warhead hit a designated target within the set timeframe,” the Russian Defense Ministry statement said. “This test launch was intended to confirm technical characteristics of the missile, as well as to check the safety of the launch procedures and equipment.” Tactical training exercises of Air Defense Forces at Kapustin Yar range. Troops prepare the anti-aircraft missile system S-300V to detect and destroy air targets. (RIA Novosti / Kirill Braga) The launch was the third successful test of the prototype ICBM. The development of a new solid-fuel ICBM was officially announced in 2012, and is set to gradually replace the existing Topol-M and later the recently developed Yars missile complex. Strategic Missile Forces expect to finalize testing by the end of 2013 and put the new missile into production in 2014. Russian Deputy Prime Minister Dmitry Rogozin welcomed the test, calling the new ICBM a “missile defense killer… Neither current nor future American missile defense systems will be able to prevent that missile from hitting a target dead on.” Russian Deputy Prime Minister Dmitry Rogozin. (RIA Novosti / Sergey Mamontov) Russia maintains at least 58 silo-based Soviet-made P36M (‘SS-18 Satan’ NATO classification) ballistic missiles, believed to be the most powerful in the world with up to 10 megaton-class warheads. The Strategic Missile Forces have 160 mobile Topol-M (‘SS-25 Sickle’) missile systems, 50 silo-based and 18 road-mobile Topol-M (‘SS-27 Sickle B’) systems, and 18 RS-24 Yars systems. In recent years, two missile divisions were rearmed with the newest Topol-M and Yars systems, and more will follow in 2013. The Defense Ministry is also preparing to introduce the latest automated battle management system (ASBU), enabling rapid retargeting of ICBMs. Russia sped up development of new intercontinental ballistic missile systems after the US announced plans to continue deploying its missile defense system in Eastern Europe, near Russian borders. Tactical exercises of the Air Defense Forces at Kapustin Yar range. Anti-aircraft S-300V missile system. (RIA Novosti / Kirill Braga) The issue of the US missile shield in Europe has become a major stumbling block in Russia-US relations. Moscow has demanded legal guarantees from Washington that missile defense systems deployed in Europe would not target Russia’s strategic nuclear deterrence capabilities. But Washington refused, citing a need to protect Europe from ‘rogue states’ like Iran and North Korea. In mid-March of 2013, Washington attempted to engage Moscow in new talks about further nuclear arms reduction, after presidents Barack Obama and Dmitry Medvedev agreed to reduce their nuclear stocks with the New START arms reduction treaty. The US said it would no longer deploy SM-3 IIB ballistic missile interceptors in Poland until 2022. Nevertheless, Moscow still demands legally binding guarantees from Washington that the system’s intentions are peaceful. On Monday, US Secretary of State John Kerry met with the Polish Foreign Minister, and committed to deploy missile defenses in Poland by 2018 as planned. “We are on track to deploy a missile defense site in Poland by 2018 as part of NATO’s modernized approach to our security,” Kerry said. http://rt.com/news/missile-defense-killer-prototype-411/ Share this: Share on Reddit (Opens in new window) Reddit Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Tumblr (Opens in new window) Tumblr Share on Pinterest (Opens in new window) Pinterest Share on LinkedIn (Opens in new window) LinkedIn Print (Opens in new window) Print Like Loading... ‹ Turkey protest turns Massive – Besiktas, Galatasaray, Fenerbahce… fans join forces Spy program shows just how well US knows its people › Categories: Military Intelligence Tags: Intercontinental ballistic missile , Ministry of Defence (Russia) , Missile , Missile defense , Moscow , RIA Novosti , Russia , United States Related Articles For Nearly Two Decades the Nuclear Launch Code at all Minuteman Silos in the United States Was 00000000 Compromised Code Names, Operations and Equipment / Recent and in progress ( Updated 12:37PM PST / 27OCT2013 ) Secret NATO manual accidentally sent to Scottish fishermen Guarded from terrorists by Royal Navy sub and 50 commandos…the UK ghost ships with enough nuclear fuel for 80 missiles Now Archiving and Organizing Historical Data Biologically Wired Differently Conservatives and Liberals Historical Hacking Archive Psionic / Psychic Warfare Archives Search Articles Translator Follow Blog via Email Join 1,878 other subscribers Top Trending Articles (Last 48 hours) The million-year-old family? https://www.dw.com/en/trump-s-us-super-i.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5Nz4j Donald Trump (left) named Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton (right) as his AI Czar Image: Alex Brandon/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement "Bigger than the Industrial Revolution and the internet" — US President Donald Trump used a comparison borrowed from "many others" to describe artificial intelligence (AI) in his announcement of a "Super Intelligence Force." The president's move to address the rapid development of the AI industry came after he met with top AI executives at the end of September — and a month before midterm elections in November. Trump has faced intensifying pressure and warnings from business and political leaders about the mostly unregulated technology . The name echoes Trump's September executive order renaming "Artificial Intelligence" as "Super intelligence" (SI) . Jay Clayton, the director of national security and the president's new AI czar , is the task force leader. The task force will coordinate the government's effort "to ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence," Trump said, and "will protect the interests, and improve the lives, of all Americans." How US, China could end the AI race To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Trump has made it clear he does not want regulation to "stifle" progress in the SI industry, and a reported charter for the group says it will work to prevent "overregulation and regulatory capture." What the Super Intelligence Force will do The White House has not released any information about the Super Intelligence Force, but a copy of a charter detailing the group's responsibilities was reported in The Wall Street Journal and Politico . The reported document shows the task force's scope is broad, but it names biosecurity and threats to the water supply as areas of focus. Recent cyberattacks have targeted critical infrastructure in the US. Who is trying to hack the US water supply? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video The group is to work with some of the most important US government agencies, including the Pentagon, the Justice Department, the Department of Homeland Security and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC), to develop recommendations for new laws to improve government responses. A legal requirement for AI labs to notify the government of "breaches, hacks and jailbreaks" is to be considered, as well as the potential for automatic alerts. "Though the labs are ultimately responsible for the risks and opportunities that their models amplify and accelerate, it is the role of the federal government to recognize and understand this era of change and to enforce our nation’s laws so that the fundamental principles of our Republic are safeguarded and advanced," the reported document says. The charter's remit includes financial services, energy infrastructure, transportation, agriculture and emergency services. Trump said the task force would coordinate the government's engagement with consumers, public interest groups and religious organizations, as well as critical infrastructure providers and AI companies, though some critics noted the omission of workers. The task force has 120 days to deliver a report on the risks of AI, focusing on potential threats to civil liberties, cybersecurity, standards for advanced models and the impacts of possible overregulation. Jay Clayton has been named the chair of Trump's newly announced Super Intelligence Force Image: Ken Cedeno/AFP Who is on the Super Intelligence Force? Clayton, whom Trump named AI czar in early October, is to chair the task force. He told The Wall Street Journal he expected AI mechanisms to be "developed in dialogue," citing risk models the Securities and Exchange Commission, which he headed during Trump's first presidential term, and the Federal Reserve developed for the financial industry. The reported charter also named three task force vice chairs: Andrew Ferguson, chairman of the FTC Emil Michael, undersecretary of defense for research and engineering Scott Kupor, director of the Office of Personnel Management Ferguson is expected to oversee consumer interests and advocacy groups, according to the reported charter. His inclusion comes as the FTC investigates OpenAI, Anthropic and METR over rogue AI agents with potentially nefarious agendas. Michael, a former tech consultant who sat on Perplexity AI's advisory board, is to oversee coordination with AI companies. Kupor is responsible for coordination with critical infrastructure providers and other industry stakeholders. Key members of Trump's Cabinet, including Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, are also on the task force. The reported charter also listed David Sacks, Trump's former AI czar, and Condoleezza Rice, former secretary of state under President George W. Bush, as external members. Former White House AI Czar David Sacks, seen here at the 2024 Republican National Convention, is reportedly an external participant in Trump's new Super Intelligence taskforce Image: Ron Sachs/CNP/Sipa USA/picture alliance The task force is to report findings and recommendations to Trump and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles. Response to the task force According to Politico , several key Republicans were not briefed on plans for the Super Intelligence Force before Trump's announcement. The task force comes as leading Republican Senators prepare major AI legislation intended to mitigate the risks AI poses. Democrats have criticized the president, with Lori Trahan, a member of the House of Representatives, telling CNN that Trump was "just talking about an AI force without any sort of durable strategy on how to do that through congressional authorization," which felt more like a delay tactic. "We should be passing legislation and guardrails around the frontier labs. And this doesn't do any of that," Trahan said. Josh Gottheimer, another Democratic representative, told Politico he was also skeptical of Trump's motives. "If this is the president waking up, realizing that AI risks aren’t a hoax, and is taking concrete action to protect America, then great," Gottheimer said. "If this is just a PR diversion and an attempt to protect his family’s investments, then I have a massive problem." Taiwan: Deadly Typhoon Champi brings travel chaos and school closures Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 23/10/2026 - 9:30 GMT+2 Towering waves crashed against Taiwan's coastline as Typhoon Champi swept past the island on Friday, leaving one person dead, 94 injured and hundreds of flights cancelled. … More In Keelung , enormous waves crashed against the shore, while emergency workers cleared fallen branches and debris from streets in the capital. One person was killed after being swept away by waves on Liuqiu island on Thursday, while 94 others were injured . ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT Schools and offices closed , while 931 flights were cancelled , including all 262 domestic services and 669 international flights. At Taipei's Songshan Airport , departure counters stood empty and stranded passengers rested beneath screens displaying cancellations. Champi had weakened from peak sustained winds of 298 km/h earlier in the week to 155 km/h as it approached Taiwan. Authorities evacuated nearly 1,300 people from vulnerable mountainous areas and urged coastal residents to stay indoors and avoid dangerous roads. The storm's centre was forecast to remain offshore before moving north towards Japan's southwestern islands , where one person was injured and nearly 2,000 homes lost power on Ishigaki. The Philippines also suspended ferry services and flights in affected areas, while residents of Cagayan province were evacuated as a precaution. https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/russia-la.text: 1 Share Emily Wright Updated Tue, October 13, 2026 at 11:23 AM UTC Russia launches devastating strikes on Ukraine - WW3 fears soar over NATO territory attack (Image: AP Photo/Andrii Marienko) Russian strikes came dangerously close to the border, sparking concerns over a direct threat to NATO airspace. World War 3 fears have grown after Russia unleashed a massive barrage of ballistic missiles and strike drones across Ukraine , triggering emergency security alerts across eastern NATO territory. The overnight assault prompted Poland's Government Centre for Security (RCB) to issue an urgent warning to residents in the southeastern Lublin and Subcarpathian voivodeships (provinces). The alert warned citizens that Polish military jets had been scrambled as Russian strikes edged dangerously close to the border, sparking concerns over a direct threat to NATO airspace. The aerial bombardment claimed at least two lives and injured 12 in Ukraine, targeting vital transport infrastructure and warehouses. At the same time, tensions spiked in the Black Sea after a suspected Russian drone attack hit two merchant vessels off the coast of NATO member Bulgaria, sinking one ship and forcing emergency rescues. With strikes striking near NATO borders and maritime routes, world leaders are closely monitoring the threat of a potential escalation under Article 5 - the alliance's collective defence clause. Ukrainian firefighters extinguish a blaze at the site of a Russian drone strike (Image: AFP via Getty Images) Russian munitions brought down a stairwell of an apartment building in Kharkiv on the evening of 12 October, and rescuers recovered three bodies from the rubble overnight, local authorities reported. Ukrainian firefighters extinguish a blaze at the site of a Russian drone strike (Image: AFP via Getty Images) Survivors described fire, falling glass and pets left behind. The strike came days after Washington waived sanctions on Russian diesel, as it expects Kyiv to stop hitting Russian refineries. Ukrainian firefighters extinguish a blaze at the site of a Russian drone strike (Image: AP Photo/Andrii Marienko) Russia has been striking Ukraine's cities every day as it readies a winter campaign against Ukrainian infrastructure, while its oil exports keep bringing in the money that pays for the drones and missiles. Rescuers evacuate an injured civilian after a residential building was hit following a Russian attac (Image: AP Photo/Andrii Marienko) Over 24 hours, Russian attacks killed three people in Kharkiv and injured 37, including two children treated for acute stress. Russian drone attack on Kyiv leaves 3 injured (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images) Larysa Maksimenko had just put her bedridden husband to sleep when the strike hit, she told Suspilne Kharkiv. She suffered a head wound and burns. "I went to the kitchen to switch on the kettle for myself, to have some coffee. I [realised] I'm on fire. Then glass fell on me. I came to, and I'm buried under everything. All covered in blood," she said. The window bars were broken and medics carried her husband out through the window. Russian drone attack on Kyiv leaves 3 injured (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images) Viacheslav Chibitko, who lives on the second floor next to the collapsed entrance, saw a flash and then everything blew out. He managed to get his three dogs out, but five cats remain inside. A drone engine is seen at the site of a Russian drone strike on a residential building in Kharkiv (Image: SERGEY KOZLOV/EPA/Shutterstock) A drone engine is seen at the site of a Russian drone strike on a residential building in Kharkiv, northeastern Ukraine on October 12, amid the ongoing Russian invasion. At least 12 people, including one child, were injured in a Russian drone strike on a residential area in Kharkiv, according to the State Emergency Service report. Chelsea-3 (Image: VesselFinder) A suspected Russian drone attack hit two ships off the coast of Bulgaria in the Black Sea, sinking one of the vessels. Bulgaria's prime minister, Rumen Radev, said the Ukrainian-owned Chelsea 3 was sailing under the Maltese flag when it was hit by three drones some 18 nautical miles (20 miles) off the Bulgarian coast at around 1.30am (11.30pm BST) on Tuesday. Its crew - seven Ukrainians and eight Azerbaijanis - were rescued and safely transported to the port of Varna. Five crew members received medical assistance, but no one was seriously injured. A second ship, the AZOV CONCORD, flying the flag of St Kitts and Nevis, was attacked about 17 nautical miles (19 miles) from the village of Krapets in north-eastern Bulgaria and sank. One sailor was rescued.
